356	          tcb->entry.main = (main_t)nx_idle_trampoline;
357	        }
358	      else
359	        {
360	          tcb->start      = nx_start;
361	          tcb->entry.main = (main_t)nx_start;
362	        }
363	
364	      tcb->task_state = TSTATE_TASK_RUNNING;
365	      tcb->lockcount  = 1;
366	      tcb->refs       = 1;
367	
368	#if CONFIG_TASK_NAME_SIZE > 0
369	      snprintf(tcb->name, CONFIG_TASK_NAME_SIZE, "CPU%d IDLE", i);

810	void nx_start(void)
811	{
812	#ifdef CONFIG_SMP
813	  int i;
814	#endif

816	  /* Boot up is complete */

818	  g_nx_initstate = OSINIT_BOOT;
819	  sched_trace_begin();
820	  sinfo("Entry\n");

822	#ifdef CONFIG_DEBUG_FEATURES
823	  up_putc('F');  /* Entering nx_start */
824	#endif

827	
828	  tasklist_initialize();
829	
830	#ifdef CONFIG_DEBUG_FEATURES
831	  up_putc('G');  /* After tasklist_initialize */
832	#endif
833

835	
836	  memory_initialize();
837

840	#endif

842	  /* MCU-specific hardware is initialized */
843	
844	  hardware_initialize();
845	
846	#ifdef CONFIG_DEBUG_FEATURES
847	  up_putc('I');  /* After hardware_initialize */
848	#endif

850	  /* Setup for Multi-Tasking ************************************************/
851	
852	  /* Announce that the CPU0 IDLE task has started */
853	
854	  sched_note_start(&this_cpu_var(g_idletcb));
855	
856	  /* Initialize stdio for the IDLE task of each CPU */
857	
858	  /* Create stdout, stderr, stdin on the CPU0 IDLE task.  These
859	   * will be inherited by all of the threads created by the CPU0
860	   * IDLE task.
861	   */
862

864	
865	#ifdef CONFIG_DEBUG_FEATURES
866	  up_putc('J');  /* After group_setupidlefiles */
867	#endif

869	#ifdef CONFIG_SMP
870	  for (i = 1; i < CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS; i++)
871	    {
872	      /* Clone stdout, stderr, stdin from the CPU0 IDLE task. */
873	
874	      DEBUGVERIFY(group_setuptaskfiles(&per_cpu_var_smp(g_idletcb, i),
875	                                        NULL, true));
876	    }
877	
878	  /* Start all CPUs *********************************************************/
879	
880	  /* A few basic sanity checks */
881	
882	  DEBUGASSERT(this_cpu() == 0);
883	
884	  /* Then start the other CPUs */
885	
886	  DEBUGVERIFY(nx_smp_start());
887	
888	#endif /* CONFIG_SMP */
889	
890	  /* Bring Up the System ****************************************************/
891	
892	  /* The OS is fully initialized and we are beginning multi-tasking */
893	
894	  g_nx_initstate = OSINIT_OSREADY;
895	  sched_trace_mark("OSREADY");
896	
897	  /* Create initial tasks and bring-up the system */
898	
899	#ifdef CONFIG_DEBUG_FEATURES
900	  up_putc('K');  /* Before nx_bringup */
901	#endif
902	
903	  nx_bringup();
904	
905	#ifdef CONFIG_DEBUG_FEATURES
906	  up_putc('L');  /* After nx_bringup (should not return normally) */
907	#endif
908	
909	  /* Enter to idleloop */
910	
911	  g_nx_initstate = OSINIT_IDLELOOP;
912	  sched_trace_mark("IDLELOOP");
913	
914	  /* Let other threads have access to the memory manager */
915	
916	  sched_trace_end();
917	  sched_unlock();
918	
919	  /* The IDLE Loop **********************************************************/
920	
921	  /* When control is return to this point, the system is idle. */
922	
923	  sinfo("CPU0: Beginning Idle Loop\n");
924	#ifndef CONFIG_DISABLE_IDLE_LOOP
925	  for (; ; )
926	    {
927	      /* Perform any processor-specific idle state operations */
928	
929	      up_idle();
930	    }
931	#endif
932	}

541	#endif

40	/****************************************************************************
41	 * Name:  nxsched_add_readytorun
42	 *
43	 * Description:
44	 *   This function adds a TCB to the ready to run list.  If the currently
45	 *   active task has preemption disabled and the new TCB would cause this
46	 *   task to be pre-empted, the new task is added to the g_pendingtasks list
47	 *   instead.  The pending tasks will be made ready-to-run when preemption is
48	 *   unlocked.
49	 *
50	 * Input Parameters:
51	 *   btcb - Points to the blocked TCB that is ready-to-run
52	 *
53	 * Returned Value:
54	 *   true if the currently active task (the head of the ready-to-run list)
55	 *   has changed.
56	 *
57	 * Assumptions:
58	 * - The caller has established a critical section before calling this
59	 *   function (calling sched_lock() first is NOT a good idea -- use
60	 *   enter_critical_section()).
61	 * - The caller has already removed the input rtcb from whatever list it
62	 *   was in.
63	 * - The caller handles the condition that occurs if the head of the
64	 *   ready-to-run list is changed.
65	 *
66	 ****************************************************************************/
67	
68	#ifndef CONFIG_SMP
69	bool nxsched_add_readytorun(FAR struct tcb_s *btcb)
70	{
71	  FAR struct tcb_s *rtcb = this_task();
72	  bool ret;
73	
74	  /* Check if pre-emption is disabled for the current running task and if
75	   * the new ready-to-run task would cause the current running task to be
76	   * pre-empted.  NOTE that IRQs disabled implies that pre-emption is
77	   * also disabled.
78	   */
79	
80	  if (rtcb->lockcount > 0 && rtcb->sched_priority < btcb->sched_priority)
81	    {
82	      /* Yes.  Preemption would occur!  Add the new ready-to-run task to the
83	       * g_pendingtasks task list for now.
84	       */
85	
86	      nxsched_add_prioritized(btcb, list_pendingtasks());
87	      btcb->task_state = TSTATE_TASK_PENDING;
88	      ret = false;
89	    }
90	
91	  /* Otherwise, add the new task to the ready-to-run task list */
92	
93	  else if (nxsched_add_prioritized(btcb, list_readytorun()))
94	    {
95	      /* The new btcb was added at the head of the ready-to-run list.  It
96	       * is now the new active task!
97	       */
98	
99	      DEBUGASSERT(rtcb->lockcount == 0 && !is_idle_task(btcb));
100	
101	      btcb->task_state = TSTATE_TASK_RUNNING;
102	      btcb->flink->task_state = TSTATE_TASK_READYTORUN;
103	      up_update_task(btcb);
104	      ret = true;
105	    }
106	  else
107	    {
108	      /* The new btcb was added in the middle of the ready-to-run list */
109	
110	      btcb->task_state = TSTATE_TASK_READYTORUN;
111	      ret = false;
112	    }
113	
114	  return ret;
115	}
116	
117	#else /* !CONFIG_SMP */

119	/****************************************************************************
120	 * Name:  nxsched_switch_running
121	 *
122	 * Description:
123	 *   This function switches the head of the current CPU's assigned tasks
124	 *   list to the TCB given as parameter. The idle task is not switched out.
125	 *   If the running task can't be swapped out, the btcb is pushed to
126	 *   the ready-to-run list.
127	 *
128	 * Input Parameters:
129	 *   cpu          - Always this_cpu(). Given as argument only for
130	 *                  optimization
131	 *   switch_equal - When true, switch away a task of equal priority compared
132	 *                  to the pending one
133	 *
134	 * Returned Value:
135	 *   true if the currently active task is switched
136	 *
137	 * Assumptions:
138	 * - The caller has established a critical section
139	 * - The caller has already removed the input rtcb from whatever list it
140	 *   was in.
141	 * - The caller handles the condition that occurs if the head of the
142	 *   assigned tasks list has changed.
143	 *
144	 ****************************************************************************/
145	
146	bool nxsched_switch_running(int cpu, bool switch_equal)
147	{
148	  FAR struct tcb_s *rtcb = current_task(cpu);
149	  int sched_priority = rtcb->sched_priority;
150	  FAR struct tcb_s *btcb;
151	  bool ret = false;
152	
153	  DEBUGASSERT(cpu == this_cpu());
154	
155	  if (nxsched_islocked_tcb(rtcb))
156	    {
157	      return false;
158	    }
159	
160	  if (switch_equal && sched_priority > 0)
161	    {
162	      sched_priority--;
163	    }
164	
165	  /* If there is a task in readytorun list, which is eglible to run on this
166	   * CPU, and has higher priority than the current task,
167	   * switch the current task to that one.
168	   */
169	
170	  for (btcb = (FAR struct tcb_s *)dq_peek(list_readytorun());
171	       btcb && btcb->sched_priority > sched_priority;
172	       btcb = btcb->flink)
173	    {
174	      /* Check if the task found in ready-to-run list is allowed to run on
175	       * this CPU. TCB_FLAG_CPU_LOCKED may be used to override affinity. If
176	       * the flag is set, assume that btcb->cpu is valid, and it is the only
177	       * CPU on which the btcb can run.
178	       */
179	
180	      if (CPU_ISSET(cpu, &btcb->affinity) &&
181	          ((btcb->flags & TCB_FLAG_CPU_LOCKED) == 0 || btcb->cpu == cpu))
182	        {
183	          /* Found a task, remove it from ready-to-run list */
184	
185	          dq_rem((FAR struct dq_entry_s *)btcb, list_readytorun());
186	
187	          if (!is_idle_task(rtcb))
188	            {
189	              /* Put currently running task back to ready-to-run list */
190	
191	              rtcb->task_state = TSTATE_TASK_READYTORUN;
192	              nxsched_add_prioritized(rtcb, list_readytorun());
193	            }
194	          else
195	            {
196	              rtcb->task_state = TSTATE_TASK_ASSIGNED;
197	            }
198	
199	          per_cpu_var_smp(g_assignedtasks, cpu) = btcb;
200	          up_update_task(btcb);
201	
202	          btcb->cpu = cpu;
203	          btcb->task_state = TSTATE_TASK_RUNNING;
204	          ret = true;
205	          break;
206	        }
207	    }
208	
209	  return ret;
210	}

214	 *
215	 * Description:
216	 *   This function adds a TCB to one of the ready to run lists. The list
217	 *   will be:
218	 *
219	 *   1. The g_readytorun list if the task is ready-to-run but not running
220	 *      and not assigned to a CPU.
221	 *   2. The g_assignedtask[cpu] list if the task is running or if has been
222	 *      assigned to a CPU.
223	 *
224	 *   If the currently active task has preemption disabled and the new TCB
225	 *   would cause this task to be pre-empted, the new task is added to the
226	 *   g_pendingtasks list instead.  The pending tasks will be made
227	 *   ready-to-run when preemption isunlocked.
228	 *

230	 *   btcb - Points to the blocked TCB that is ready-to-run
231	 *
232	 * Returned Value:
233	 *   true if the currently active task (the head of the ready-to-run list)
234	 *   has changed.
235	 *
236	 * Assumptions:
237	 * - The caller has established a critical section before calling this
238	 *   function (calling sched_lock() first is NOT a good idea -- use
239	 *   enter_critical_section()).
240	 * - The caller has already removed the input rtcb from whatever list it
241	 *   was in.
242	 * - The caller handles the condition that occurs if the head of the
243	 *   ready-to-run list has changed.
244	 *
245	 ****************************************************************************/
246	
247	bool nxsched_add_readytorun(FAR struct tcb_s *btcb)
248	{
249	  bool doswitch = false;
250	  int target_cpu = btcb->flags & TCB_FLAG_CPU_LOCKED ? btcb->cpu :
251	    nxsched_select_cpu(btcb->affinity);
252	  FAR struct tcb_s *tcb = current_task(target_cpu);
253	
254	  /* Add the btcb to the ready to run list, and try to run it on the target
255	   * CPU
256	   */
257	
258	  btcb->task_state = TSTATE_TASK_READYTORUN;
259	  nxsched_add_prioritized(btcb, list_readytorun());
260	
261	  /* In some cases, such as setaffinity, cpu need to be used. */
262	
263	  btcb->cpu = target_cpu;
264	  if (tcb->sched_priority < btcb->sched_priority)
265	    {
266	      doswitch = nxsched_deliver_task(this_cpu(), target_cpu,
267	                                      SWITCH_HIGHER);
268	    }
269	
270	  return doswitch;
271	}
272	
273	#endif /* CONFIG_SMP */

69	  irqstate_t flags;
70	
71	  flags = enter_critical_section();
72	  tcb = nxsched_get_tcb(pid);
73	
74	  if (!tcb || tcb->task_state == TSTATE_TASK_INVALID ||
75	      (atomic_read(&tcb->flags) & TCB_FLAG_EXIT_PROCESSING) != 0)

105	 *
106	 * Input Parameters:
107	 *   tcb - The TCB of the currently executing task
108	 *   ticks - The number of ticks that have elapsed on the interval timer.
109	 *   noswitches - True: Can't do context switches now.
110	 *
111	 * Returned Value:
112	 *   The number if ticks remaining until the next time slice expires.
113	 *   CLOCK_MAX is returned if there is no time slicing (i.e., the task at
114	 *   the head of the ready-to-run list does not support round robin
115	 *   scheduling).
116	 *
117	 *   The value one may returned under certain circumstances that probably
118	 *   can't happen.  The value one is the minimal timer setup and it means
119	 *   that a context switch is needed now, but cannot be performed because
120	 *   noswitches == true.
121	 *

123	 *   - Interrupts are disabled
124	 *   - The task associated with TCB uses the round robin scheduling
125	 *     policy
126	 *

130	                                   bool noswitches)

132	  FAR struct tcb_s *ptcb;  /* Pointer to the next ready-to-run TCB */
133	  clock_t ret;
134	  int decr;

137	   * than the timeslice value, then we ignore any excess amount.
138	   *

140	   * event seems to be possible, perhaps in cases where pre-emption has been

142	   * few ticks in the slicing because the excess amount is not handled.

160	       * as soon as possible and we can perform this action in the normal
161	       * timer expiration context.
162	       *
163	       * This is kind of kludge, but I am not to concerned because I hope
164	       * that the situation is impossible or at least could only occur on
165	       * rare corner-cases.
166	       */

168	      if (noswitches)
169	        {
170	          ret = 0;
171	        }

78	                               size_t count)
79	{
80	  uint8_t *d = dest + count - 1;
81	  const uint8_t *s = src + count - 1;
82	
83	  if (dest <= src)
84	    {
85	      _err("dest and src should overlap");

106	static void sg2000_copy_ramdisk(void)
107	{
108	  const char *header = "-rom1fs-";
109	  const uint8_t *limit = (uint8_t *)g_idle_topstack + (256 * 1024);
110	  uint8_t *ramdisk_addr = NULL;
111	  uint8_t *addr;
112	  uint32_t size;
113	
114	  /* After _edata, search for "-rom1fs-". This is the RAM Disk Address.
115	   * Limit search to 256 KB after Idle Stack Top.
116	   */
117	
118	  binfo("_edata=%p, _sbss=%p, _ebss=%p, idlestack_top=%p\n",
119	        (void *)_edata, (void *)_sbss, (void *)_ebss,
120	        (void *)g_idle_topstack);
121	  for (addr = _edata; addr < limit; addr++)
122	    {
123	      if (memcmp(addr, header, strlen(header)) == 0)
124	        {
125	          ramdisk_addr = addr;
126	          break;
127	        }
128	    }
129	
130	  /* Stop if RAM Disk is missing */
131	
132	  binfo("ramdisk_addr=%p\n", ramdisk_addr);
133	  if (ramdisk_addr == NULL)
134	    {
135	      _err("Missing RAM Disk. Check the initrd padding.");
136	      PANIC();
137	    }
138	
139	  /* RAM Disk must be after Idle Stack, to prevent overwriting */
140	
141	  if (ramdisk_addr <= (uint8_t *)g_idle_topstack)
142	    {
143	      const size_t pad = (size_t)g_idle_topstack - (size_t)ramdisk_addr;
144	      _err("RAM Disk must be after Idle Stack. Increase initrd padding "
145	            "by %ul bytes.", pad);
146	      PANIC();
147	    }

149	  /* Read the Filesystem Size from the next 4 bytes (Big Endian) */
150

152	         (ramdisk_addr[10] << 8) + ramdisk_addr[11] + 0x1f0;
153	  binfo("size=%d\n", size);
154	
155	  /* Filesystem Size must be less than RAM Disk Memory Region */
156	
157	  if (size > (size_t)__ramdisk_size)

160	            size - (size_t)__ramdisk_size);

  /* Exported Symbols */

  .section .text
  .global __start

__start:

  /* DO NOT MODIFY. Image Header expected by Linux bootloaders.
   *
   * This `li` instruction has no meaningful effect except that
   * its opcode forms the magic "MZ" signature of a PE/COFF file
   * that is required for UEFI applications.
   *
   * Some bootloaders check the magic "MZ" to see if the image is a valid
   * Linux image. But modifying the bootLoader is unnecessary unless we
   * need to do a customized secure boot. So we just put "MZ" in the
   * header to make the bootloader happy.
   */

  c.li    s4, -13              /* Magic Signature "MZ" (2 bytes) */
  j       real_start           /* Jump to Kernel Start (2 bytes) */
  .long   0                    /* Executable Code padded to 8 bytes */
  .quad   0x200000             /* Image load offset from start of RAM */
  .quad   _ebss - __start      /* Effective size of kernel image */
  .quad   0                    /* Kernel flags, little-endian */
  .long   2                    /* Version of this header */
  .long   0                    /* Reserved */
  .quad   0                    /* Reserved */
  .ascii  "RISCV\x00\x00\x00"  /* Magic number, "RISCV" (8 bytes) */
  .ascii  "RSC\x05"            /* Magic number 2, "RSC\x05" (4 bytes) */
  .long   0                    /* Reserved for PE COFF offset */

real_start:

  /* Load the number of CPUs that the kernel supports */

#ifdef CONFIG_SMP
  li   t1, CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS
#else
  li   t1, 1
#endif

  /* If a0 (hartid) >= t1 (the number of CPUs), stop here */

  blt  a0, t1, 3f
  csrw CSR_SIE, zero
  wfi

  riscv_set_inital_sp SG2000_IDLESTACK_BASE, SMP_STACK_SIZE, a0

  /* Disable all interrupts (i.e. timer, external) in sie */

  csrw CSR_SIE, zero

  la   t0, __trap_vec
  csrw CSR_STVEC, t0

  /* Jump to sg2000_start */

  jal  x1, sg2000_start

  /* We shouldn't return from _start */

  .global _init
  .global _fini

_init:
_fini:

  /* These don't have to do anything since we use init_array/fini_array. */

## Memory Management Architecture Overview

OpenVela (based on NuttX RTOS) implements a sophisticated multi-layered memory management system with several allocation strategies optimized for different use cases.

---

## 1. Heap Management (mm_heap)

### Core Data Structures

**File: `/home/wsb/openvela/nuttx/mm/mm_heap/mm.h`**

The heap is managed through a doubly-linked list of free nodes with the following key structures:

- **`struct mm_allocnode_s`**: Represents an allocated memory chunk
  - `preceding`: Size of the physically preceding chunk
  - `size`: Size of current chunk with allocation status bits (bit 0 = allocated, bit 1 = previous free)
  - Optional fields for PID recording, sequence numbers, and stack backtrace

- **`struct mm_freenode_s`**: Represents a free memory chunk
  - Contains `flink` and `blink` pointers for doubly-linked list management
  - Sorted by size for efficient allocation

- **`struct mm_heap_s`**: Main heap structure containing:
  - `mm_lock`: Recursive mutex for thread-safe access
  - `mm_heapsize`, `mm_curused`, `mm_maxused`: Statistics tracking
  - `mm_heapstart[]`, `mm_heapend[]`: Region boundaries (supports multiple regions)
  - `mm_nodelist[]`: Array of free node lists indexed by size (power-of-2 buckets)
  - `delay`: Per-CPU delayed free lists for interrupt context
  - `mm_mpool`: Optional mempool integration

### Heap Initialization

**File: `/home/wsb/openvela/nuttx/mm/mm_heap/mm_initialize.c`**

The initialization process:
1. Allocates or reserves space for `mm_heap_s` structure
2. Initializes the free node array (`mm_nodelist[]`) with linked sentinel nodes
3. Creates a recursive mutex for thread safety
4. Calls `mm_addregion()` to add the initial memory region

`mm_addregion()`:
- Aligns the heap start and end addresses
- Creates guard nodes at the beginning and end (allocated nodes to prevent boundary overflow)
- Creates one large free node containing all available memory
- Adds the free node to the appropriate size-indexed list
- Registers with KASAN (Kernel Address Sanitizer) if enabled

### Memory Allocation Algorithm (First-Fit with Size Buckets)

**File: `/home/wsb/openvela/nuttx/mm/mm_heap/mm_malloc.c`**

The allocation algorithm:
1. **Size bucket selection**: Uses `mm_size2ndx()` to convert size to an index in the nodelist array. The index is calculated using `flsl()` (find last set bit) to get a logarithmic bucket index.

2. **Free list search**: Searches the appropriate bucket and larger buckets for a free node >= requested size. The lists are ordered by size, so the first match is the best fit within that bucket.

3. **Node splitting**: If the found node is larger than needed by at least `MM_MIN_CHUNK`, it splits the node:
   - Creates a remainder free node
   - Updates the allocated node's size
   - Adjusts the `preceding` field of the next physical node
   - Adds the remainder back to the free list

4. **Allocation**: Sets the `MM_ALLOC_BIT` in the node's size field and returns a pointer to the usable memory (after the header).

### Memory Deallocation with Coalescing

**File: `/home/wsb/openvela/nuttx/mm/mm_heap/mm_free.c`**

The free process:
1. **Delayed free mechanism**: If `CONFIG_MM_FREE_DELAYCOUNT_MAX > 0`, memory is added to a per-CPU delay list instead of being freed immediately. This is critical for:
   - Interrupt context where mutex acquisition is unsafe
   - SMP systems to reduce lock contention
   - Double-free detection using magic values

2. **Immediate free** (`mm_forcefree()`):
   - Clears the `MM_ALLOC_BIT`
   - **Forward coalescing**: If the next physical node is free, merges with it
   - **Backward coalescing**: If the previous physical node is free, merges with it
   - Adds the merged node back to the appropriate free list bucket

3. **Double-free detection**: Uses magic values (`~(uintptr_t)mem`) stored in the delay node to detect double-frees, with list traversal verification to avoid false positives.

---

## 2. TLSF Allocator (Two-Level Segregated Fit)

**File: `/home/wsb/openvela/nuttx/mm/tlsf/mm_tlsf.c`**

OpenVela provides an alternative allocator based on TLSF (Two-Level Segregated Fit), which is selected via configuration.

### Key Characteristics:
- **O(1) allocation and deallocation time complexity**
- **Low fragmentation**: Uses a two-level segregated fit approach

**File: `/home/wsb/openvela/nuttx/mm/mempool/mempool.c`**

```c
struct mempool_s {

  size_t initialsize;    // Initial pool size
  size_t expandsize;     // Size to expand when exhausted
  size_t interruptsize;  // Reserved blocks for interrupt context
  size_t maxalloc;       // Maximum number of allocations (0 = unlimited)
  size_t nalloc;         // Current number of allocated blocks
  
  sq_queue_t queue;      // Main free block queue
  sq_queue_t iqueue;     // Interrupt-safe free block queue
  sq_queue_t equeue;     // Expansion chunk queue

  spinlock_t lock;       // Fast spinlock protection
  sem_t waitsem;         // Semaphore for blocking allocation
};
```

### Key Features:

1. **Three-tier allocation**:
   - **Normal queue** (`queue`): Main free list for regular allocations
   - **Interrupt queue** (`iqueue`): Pre-allocated blocks reserved for interrupt context (allocated from `interruptsize`)
   - **Dynamic expansion**: Allocates new chunks when queues are empty

2. **Lazy initialization**: Pools are initialized on first use via `mempool_init()`

3. **Blocking allocation**: If `wait` is set and `expandsize` is 0, `mempool_allocate()` can block on a semaphore until a block becomes available

4. **Thread safety**: Uses spinlocks for fast critical sections

5. **KASAN integration**: Blocks are poisoned when free and unpoisoned when allocated

### Allocation Flow:
```c
void *mempool_allocate(pool, timeout) {
  // Try normal queue first
  blk = remove_from_queue(&pool->queue);
  
  // If in interrupt context, try interrupt queue
  if (up_interrupt_context())
    blk = remove_from_queue(&pool->iqueue);
  
  // If still no block, expand the pool
  if (blk == NULL && pool->expandsize > 0) {
    base = pool->alloc(pool, expandsize);
    add_blocks_to_queue(&pool->queue, base, nblocks);
    blk = remove_from_queue(&pool->queue);
  }
  
  // Or wait if configured
  if (blk == NULL && pool->wait)
    nxsem_wait(&pool->waitsem);
  
  return blk;
}
```

```c
  size_t expandsize;          // Expansion size for each pool

  size_t minpoolsize;         // Minimum pool size
```

Uses binary search or arithmetic calculation to find the appropriate pool for a given size:
- If pools have uniform delta (arithmetic progression): Direct calculation
- Otherwise: Binary search through sorted pool array

When `CONFIG_MM_HEAP_MEMPOOL` is enabled:
- `mm_malloc()` first tries `mempool_multiple_alloc()` before falling back to the main allocator
- `mm_free()` first tries `mempool_multiple_free()` before falling back to the main free

**File: `/home/wsb/openvela/nuttx/mm/kmm_heap/kmm_initialize.c`**

|--------|-------------|-----------|
| Access | Per-CPU global `g_kmmheap` | Per-process or global `g_mmheap` |
| Security | Full kernel access | May have memory protection |
| SMP Support | Per-CPU heaps for scalability | May be global or per-process |

## 6. Granule-Based Allocation (mm_gran)

**File: `/home/wsb/openvela/nuttx/mm/mm_gran/mm_graninit.c`**

The granule allocator provides fixed-granularity memory allocation, typically used for DMA buffers or page-aligned memory.

### Core Structure:
```c
struct gran_s {
  uint8_t log2gran;      // Log2 of granule size (e.g., 6 = 64 bytes)
  uint8_t log2align;     // Log2 of required alignment
  uint32_t ngranules;    // Total number of granules
  uintptr_t heapstart;   // Aligned heap start
  uint32_t gat[1];       // Granule Allocation Table (bitmap)
};
```

### Key Features:

1. **Bitmap-based tracking**: Uses a Granule Allocation Table (GAT) - an array of 32-bit bitmaps where each bit represents one granule.

2. **Configurable granularity**: Granule size is 2^log2gran bytes (e.g., log2gran=6 gives 64-byte granules)

3. **Alignment support**: Memory is aligned to 2^log2align bytes

4. **Efficient search**: Uses de Bruijn sequence for fast bit scanning when hardware CLZ/CTZ instructions are unavailable

### Initialization:
```c
GRAN_HANDLE gran_initialize(heapstart, heapsize, log2gran, log2align) {
  // Calculate aligned start and number of granules
  mask = (1 << log2align) - 1;
  alignedstart = ((uintptr_t)heapstart + mask) & ~mask;
  
  ngranules = alignedsize >> log2gran;
  
  // Allocate GAT structure
  priv = kmm_zalloc(SIZEOF_GRAN_S(ngranules));
  
  priv->log2gran = log2gran;
  priv->log2align = log2align;
  priv->ngranules = ngranules;
  priv->heapstart = alignedstart;
}
```

### Allocation:
```c
void *gran_alloc(handle, size) {
  ngran = NGRANULE(gran, size);  // Convert bytes to granules
  
  gran_enter_critical();
  posi = gran_search(gran, ngran);  // Find free consecutive granules
  if (posi >= 0)
    gran_set(gran, posi, ngran);   // Mark granules as allocated
  gran_leave_critical();
  
  return gran->heapstart + (posi << gran->log2gran);
}
```

1. **Flexible heap allocation** with both traditional first-fit (with size buckets) and TLSF algorithms

```
通电 → __start 标签
```

```
sg2000_start() → sg2000_start_s() → nx_start()
```

1. **清 BSS 段**：`sg2000_clear_bss()` —— 把所有未初始化的全局变量清零，就像整理房间。

4. **关闭 MMU**：`WRITE_CSR(CSR_SATP, 0x0)` —— 先用物理地址直接访问内存。

5. **初始化 MMU 页表**：`sg2000_mm_init()` —— 建立虚拟地址到物理地址的映射表，然后开启 MMU。

6. **调用 `nx_start()`** —— 进入 NuttX 内核的正式初始化！

### 第三阶段：内核初始化（[nx_start.c](nuttx/sched/init/nx_start.c)）

`nx_start()` 是整个操作系统的"总指挥"，按顺序完成以下工作：

| 步骤 | 函数 | 做什么 |
|------|------|--------|
| 1 | `tasklist_initialize()` | 初始化任务列表、看门狗、信号量 |
| 2 | `memory_initialize()` | 初始化内核堆、用户堆、页分配器 |
| 3 | `hardware_initialize()` | 初始化文件系统、中断、时钟、网络、驱动 |
| 4 | `group_setupidlefiles()` | 设置标准输入输出（stdin/stdout/stderr） |
| 5 | `nx_bringup()` | 启动工作队列、创建第一个用户任务 |
| 6 | `up_idle()` | 进入 IDLE 循环（空闲时 CPU 执行的代码） |

```
nx_bringup()
  ├── nx_pgworker()      // 启动页填充工作线程
  ├── nx_workqueues()    // 启动高/低优先级工作队列
  └── nx_create_initthread()  // 创建 init 任务（用户空间第一个进程）
```

**通俗比喻**：就像开一家餐厅——先装修（初始化硬件），再招厨师和服务员（创建工作线程），最后开门迎客（启动 init 进程）。

---

## 二、进程调度：谁来用 CPU？

OpenVela 的调度器就像一个**严格的排队系统**，核心思想是：**优先级高的先跑，同优先级轮流跑**。

### 2.1 任务状态机

一个任务（Task）在生命周期中会经历这些状态：

```
创建(INACTIVE) → 就绪(READYTORUN) → 运行(RUNNING) → 阻塞(WAIT_SEM/WAIT_SIG)
     ↑                                                    │
     └────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### 2.2 核心数据结构：任务控制块（TCB）

每个任务都有一个 TCB（Task Control Block），就像一张"身份证"，记录着：

- **PID**：进程号
- **优先级**：`sched_priority`，数字越大优先级越高
- **状态**：当前处于哪个状态
- **栈指针**：任务的栈在哪里
- **时间片**：还剩多少 CPU 时间

### 2.3 调度策略

#### （1）优先级抢占式调度

文件：[sched_addreadytorun.c](nuttx/sched/sched/sched_addreadytorun.c)

```
高优先级任务就绪 → 立即抢占低优先级任务
```

核心逻辑：
```c
if (当前任务锁 == 0 && 新任务优先级 > 当前任务优先级) {
    // 立即切换到新任务
    切换上下文();
} else if (当前任务锁 > 0) {
    // 当前任务禁止抢占，放入 pending 队列
    放入待处理列表();
}
```

**通俗比喻**：急诊室里，病情严重的病人（高优先级）可以插队，但正在手术中的病人（lockcount > 0）不会被打断。

#### （2）轮转调度（Round-Robin）

文件：[sched_roundrobin.c](nuttx/sched/sched/sched_roundrobin.c)

对于**相同优先级**的任务，采用时间片轮转：

- 每个任务分配一个时间片（`CONFIG_RR_INTERVAL`，单位毫秒）
- 时间片用完 → 放到队尾 → 下一个同优先级任务开始
- 如果没有同优先级任务，继续运行

```c
// 时间片用完的处理
if (timeslice <= 0) {
    重置时间片();
    if (有同优先级任务等待) {
        把当前任务移到队尾();
        切换到下一个任务();
    }
}
```

**通俗比喻**：几个同样紧急的病人轮流看诊，每人限时 10 分钟，时间到了就排到队尾。

#### （3）SMP 多核调度

在多核情况下，调度器还需要决定任务在哪个 CPU 上运行：

```c
target_cpu = 任务被锁定在某个CPU ? 锁定的CPU : 选择最空闲的CPU;
```

支持 **CPU 亲和性**（Affinity）——可以指定任务只在某些 CPU 上运行。

### 2.4 调度流程图

```
任务就绪
    │
    ▼
检查是否可以抢占？ ──否──→ 放入就绪队列（按优先级排序）
    │是
    ▼
当前任务是否锁定调度？ ──是──→ 放入 pending 队列
    │否
    ▼
执行上下文切换 ──→ 新任务开始运行
```

---

## 三、内存管理：内存怎么分？

OpenVela 的内存管理就像一个**智能仓库管理系统**，有多种分配策略适应不同场景。

### 3.1 内存堆的初始化

文件：[nx_start.c:memory_initialize()](nuttx/sched/init/nx_start.c#L567)

```
memory_initialize()
  ├── kmm_initialize()     // 初始化内核堆
  ├── kumm_initialize()    // 初始化用户堆
  ├── mm_pginitialize()    // 初始化页分配器
  └── iob_initialize()     // 初始化 I/O 缓冲区
```

### 3.2 内存分配算法

#### （1）TLSF 分配器（Two-Level Segregated Fit）

文件：[mm_tlsf.c](nuttx/mm/tlsf/mm_tlsf.c)

TLSF 是 OpenVela 的**主力分配器**，特点是：

- **两级索引**：把内存块按大小分成多个"桶"
- **O(1) 分配**：不管内存多大，分配时间都是常数
- **低碎片**：通过巧妙的分桶策略减少内存浪费

```
请求 100 字节
    │
    ▼
计算属于哪个"桶" ──→ 在桶中找最合适的空闲块
    │
    ▼
找到块 ──→ 切割（如果太大）──→ 返回指针
    │
    ▼
没找到 ──→ 尝试合并相邻空闲块 ──→ 再试一次
```

#### （2）传统堆分配器

文件：[mm_malloc.c](nuttx/mm/mm_heap/mm_malloc.c)

当 TLSF 不可用时，使用传统的**首次适配（First-Fit）**算法：

```c
// 遍历空闲链表，找到第一个够大的块
for (node = 空闲链表头; node != NULL; node = node->下一个) {
    if (node->大小 >= 请求大小) {
        找到了();
        break;
    }
}
```

分配时还会做**内存对齐**（8 字节对齐），确保访问效率。

#### （3）内存池（Mempool）

文件：[mempool/](nuttx/mm/mempool/)

对于**频繁分配/释放的小对象**，使用内存池：

```
预分配一块大内存
    │
    ▼
切成固定大小的小块 ──→ 用链表串起来
    │
    ▼
需要时从链表取一块 ──→ 用完放回链表
```

**优点**：分配/释放都是 O(1)，不会产生碎片。

### 3.3 内核堆 vs 用户堆

| 特性 | 内核堆（kmm） | 用户堆（umm） |
|------|--------------|--------------|
| 管理者 | 内核 | 用户空间 |
| 访问权限 | 仅内核态 | 用户态可访问 |
| 典型用途 | 驱动、内核数据结构 | 应用程序 |

### 3.4 延迟释放机制

文件：[mm_malloc.c:free_delaylist()](nuttx/mm/mm_heap/mm_malloc.c#L60)

```c
// 释放内存时，先放入延迟队列
if (获取锁失败) {
    放入延迟释放队列();
    return;
}

// 下次分配时，先清理延迟队列
free_delaylist(heap, false);
```

**为什么需要延迟释放？** 在中断上下文中，获取内存锁可能失败，所以先把释放请求"记下来"，等下次安全时再处理。

### 3.5 MMU 页表管理

文件：[sg2000_mm_init.c](nuttx/arch/risc-v/src/sg2000/sg2000_mm_init.c)

```
物理内存布局：
┌──────────────┐ 0x00000000
│   I/O 区域    │ (设备寄存器)
├──────────────┤ 0x40000000
│   内核代码    │ (Flash)
├──────────────┤
│   内核数据    │ (RAM)
├──────────────┤
│   用户空间    │ (应用)
├──────────────┤ 0x70000000
│   中断控制器  │ (PLIC)
├──────────────┤
│   页表池     │ (Page Tables)
└──────────────┘
```

使用 **SV39 三级页表**：
- L1 → L2 → L3 → 物理页
- 每页 4KB
- 支持大页映射（2MB）

---

## 总结：三者如何协同工作？

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                      应用程序                            │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│         进程调度器（优先级 + 轮转）                      │
│    决定哪个任务获得 CPU 时间                              │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│         内存管理器（TLSF + 内存池）                      │
│    为任务分配和回收内存                                   │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│         硬件抽象层（RISC-V MMU + 中断）                  │
│    提供硬件访问接口                                       │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**一句话总结**：
- **启动流程**：从汇编到 C，从硬件初始化到创建第一个用户进程，层层递进
- **进程调度**：高优先级抢占 + 同优先级轮转，简单高效
- **内存管理**：TLSF 分配器 + 内存池 + 延迟释放，兼顾速度和碎片控制

The RISC-V boot sequence in NuttX follows a consistent pattern across all chip implementations, though the specific details vary slightly between chips. The flow is:

```

    -> C startup function (start.c)    [per-chip]
      -> nx_start()                    [common scheduler code]
```

There are two execution mode variants:
- **M-mode (Machine mode)**: The kernel runs directly in machine mode. CSRs are `mtvec`, `mstatus`, `mie`, `mepc`, `mcause`.
- **S-mode (Supervisor mode)**: The kernel runs in supervisor mode with an SBI (Supervisor Binary Interface) below it. CSRs are `stvec`, `sstatus`, `sie`, `sepc`, `scause`.

The CSR names in the code (`CSR_STATUS`, `CSR_TVEC`, `CSR_IE`, `CSR_EPC`, `CSR_CAUSE`) are abstract macros defined in `/home/wsb/openvela/nuttx/arch/risc-v/include/mode.h` that resolve to either the M-mode or S-mode variants depending on configuration.

**File pattern**: `arch/risc-v/src/<chip>/<chip>_head.S`
